english.notes:
(i) The consent of the Director of Public Prosecutions is required, section 160(4) of the Criminal Justice Act 1988 and section 1(3) of the Protection of Children Act 1978.
(ii) 'Child' means a person under 18 (section 7(6)), but see section 7(8) for the proviso in relation to pseudo-photographs.
(iii) A pseudo-photograph is an image whether made by computer graphics or otherwise which appears to be a photograph.
(iv) See also offence wordings: H1629, H2009, H2101, H2105, H2222 and H4373 for the offences of taking, making, distributing, showing, publishing, advertising such photographs which carry a greater penalty.
(v) This offence is included in Schedule 3 to the Sexual Offences Act 2003. Therefore a person convicted or cautioned for this offence must comply with the notification requirements of Part 2 of that Act.
(vi). This Offence wording has been amended by Section 41(3) of the Criminal Justice and Courts Services Act 2000 to create an either way offence, the penalty on indictment being 5 years imprisonment with effect from 11/01/01.
(vii) See Section 160(2) for defence.
(vii) Please refer to the extensive Notes in relation to this offence which are attached to the legal topic document covering section 1 of the Protection of Children Act 1978.
(viii) Sections 1A and 1B of the Protection of Children Act 1978 provides defences to the offence in specified circumstances.

other.penalty:
Either waySummary: maximum 6/12 months imprisonment and/or fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: maximum 5 years imprisonment and/or a fine.

The maximum penalty on summary conviction may be 6 or 12 months depending on the general limit in a magistrates’ court, see section 282(2) and (3) of the Criminal Justice Act 2003 and section 224(1) and (1A) of the Sentencing Act 2020.

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
